name: Lotan
overview: Lotan was a male Edomite chief, identified as the son of Seir, a prominent figure in the Edomite lineage. His leadership role as a chief in Edom marks him as a significant tribal leader within this ancient people. There are no additional notes recorded about him beyond these attributes.
namesAndTitles: The name Lotan is a proper name meaning 'of Lot,' as recorded in Genesis 36:20. There is no indication that this name was given by God, and it stands simply as his personal designation within the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Lotan as the son of Seir. Inferred relationships include Hori and Hemam as his descendants and Timna as his brother, all mentioned within the Edomite genealogy. Beyond these, no further family details are provided.
scriptureSignificance: Lotan's significance lies in his place within the Edomite tribal structure as a chief and as a son of Seir, who was the eponymous ancestor of the Edomites. His mention in the genealogies of Genesis highlights the organized tribal leadership established among the descendants of Esau. This contributes to the biblical understanding of the nations and peoples surrounding Israel, emphasizing God's sovereign orchestration of history through family lines and tribal leadership.
